messages.content: I need all pending and active mandates of users parath and bhanu

function.name: user_mandates
function.description: Fetches the mandates associated with a user based on the provided user name and the status of the mandates. This API is intended for use by partners to retrieve information about their clients' mandates. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

name.description: The full name of the partner's client for whom to fetch mandates.

status.description: The status of the mandates to be fetched.

function.name: partner_mandates
function.description: Fetches the mandates associated with a partner based on the specified status. If no status is provided, all mandates are retrieved. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

status.description: The status of the mandates to be fetched. If left empty, mandates with any status will be retrieved.

message.reasoning:
We need to call user_mandates twice? The user wants all pending and active mandates of users parath and bhanu. So we need to fetch mandates for each user with status pending or active. The function signature: user_mandates(name, status?) default active. We can call twice: one for parath, one for bhanu. But we need both statuses. We could call with status "active" and "pending". But the function only accepts one status. So we need two calls per user. Or maybe we can call with status unspecified to get active (default). Then call with status "pending". So total 4 calls. But maybe we can combine? The function only returns mandates for a single status. So we need separate calls.

Thus we should produce two calls: one for parath active, one for parath pending, same for bhanu. But the user asked "all pending and active mandates of users parath and bhanu". So we can call partner_mandates? That fetches mandates for partner. Not relevant.

Thus we need to call user_mandates twice per user. Let's do that.
